blocks.alt: Left: a table of the eleven pollutant classes with their main sources and a note on each, followed by the natural and human-made sources. Top right: the three CFC equations with the chlorine radical regenerated. Middle right: primary and secondary pollutants. Bottom: the combustion, nitrogen oxide and sulfur oxide equations with notes on carbon monoxide, N2O and PM2.5.
blocks.caption: The classes of air pollutant, their sources, the CFC attack on ozone and key equations (original diagram after topics 14.2 to 14.4.11 and Table 14.1).
blocks.long_description: Fossil fuel combustion lies behind most of the pollutant classes: carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides made at high temperature, sulfur oxides from coal and oil, unburnt hydrocarbons, and the volatile organic compounds and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons that accompany incomplete burning. Ground-level ozone is secondary, made from nitrogen oxides and volatile organics in sunlight, and chlorofluorocarbons released from aerosols and refrigerators drift to the stratosphere, where ultraviolet light frees chlorine radicals that destroy ozone over and over. Persistent organic pollutants such as PCBs and DDT resist breakdown and travel far, particulate matter comes from dust, fires and engines, and heavy metals from metallurgy, batteries and incineration.
